name: AuthLabKubernetesHardening
description: Project-owned Kubernetes hardening policy for the AuthLab deployment. It combines selected Kubescape workload controls with the AuthLab Service exposure contract.

controls.name: AuthLab Service exposure contract
controls.description: Ensures that the AuthLab Service remains an internal-only ClusterIP Service with the expected identity, selector and port contract.
controls.remediation: Restore Service/authlab in namespace authlab as a non-headless ClusterIP Service without externalIPs, ExternalName or nodePort exposure. Use the expected AuthLab selectors and a single TCP port 5000 targeting the named http container port.
controls.long_description: The AuthLab deployment is intentionally reachable only through an internal Kubernetes ClusterIP Service. External exposure fields, incorrect selectors or an unexpected port contract can bypass deployment assumptions or route traffic to unintended workloads.
controls.test: Check that Service/authlab is an internal-only ClusterIP Service using the expected AuthLab selector and port contract.

rules.name: authlab-service-exposure-contract
rules.description: Fails when a Service violates the AuthLab internal exposure, selector or port contract.
rules.remediation: Restore the expected AuthLab ClusterIP Service configuration.
rules.rule:
package armo_builtins

service_alert(service, message, paths) = result {
	result := {
		"alertMessage": sprintf(
			"Service %v/%v violates the AuthLab exposure contract: %v",
			[
				service.metadata.namespace,
				service.metadata.name,
				message
			]
		),
		"packagename": "armo_builtins",
		"alertScore": 6,
		"reviewPaths": paths,
		"failedPaths": paths,
		"fixPaths": [],
		"alertObject": {
			"k8sApiObjects": [service]
		}
	}
}

deny[msga] {
	service := input[_]
	service.kind == "Service"
	service.metadata.name != "authlab"

	msga := service_alert(
		service,
		"metadata.name must be authlab",
		["metadata.name"]
	)
}

deny[msga] {
	service := input[_]
	service.kind == "Service"
	service.metadata.namespace != "authlab"

	msga := service_alert(
		service,
		"metadata.namespace must be authlab",
		["metadata.namespace"]
	)
}

deny[msga] {
	service := input[_]
	service.kind == "Service"
	object.get(service.spec, "type", "") != "ClusterIP"

	msga := service_alert(
		service,
		"spec.type must be ClusterIP",
		["spec.type"]
	)
}

deny[msga] {
	service := input[_]
	service.kind == "Service"
	object.get(service.spec, "clusterIP", "") == "None"

	msga := service_alert(
		service,
		"headless ClusterIP is not allowed",
		["spec.clusterIP"]
	)
}

deny[msga] {
	service := input[_]
	service.kind == "Service"

	external_ips := object.get(service.spec, "externalIPs", [])
	count(external_ips) > 0

	msga := service_alert(
		service,
		"spec.externalIPs must be empty",
		["spec.externalIPs"]
	)
}

deny[msga] {
	service := input[_]
	service.kind == "Service"
	object.get(service.spec, "externalName", "") != ""

	msga := service_alert(
		service,
		"spec.externalName is not allowed",
		["spec.externalName"]
	)
}

deny[msga] {
	service := input[_]
	service.kind == "Service"

	ports := object.get(service.spec, "ports", [])
	port := ports[_]
	object.get(port, "nodePort", 0) != 0

	msga := service_alert(
		service,
		"nodePort allocation is not allowed",
		["spec.ports"]
	)
}

deny[msga] {
	service := input[_]
	service.kind == "Service"

	ports := object.get(service.spec, "ports", [])
	count(ports) != 1

	msga := service_alert(
		service,
		"exactly one Service port is required",
		["spec.ports"]

deny[msga] {
	service := input[_]
	service.kind == "Service"

	ports := object.get(service.spec, "ports", [])
	count(ports) == 1
	port := ports[0]

	msga := service_alert(
		service,
		"the Service port name must be http",
		["spec.ports[0].name"]
	)

deny[msga] {

	service.kind == "Service"

	ports := object.get(service.spec, "ports", [])
	count(ports) == 1

deny[msga] {
	service := input[_]
	service.kind == "Service"

	ports := object.get(service.spec, "ports", [])
	count(ports) == 1
	port := ports[0]

deny[msga] {

	service.kind == "Service"

	ports := object.get(service.spec, "ports", [])
	count(ports) == 1
	port := ports[0]

	object.get(port, "targetPort", "") != "http"

	msga := service_alert(
		service,
		"targetPort must reference the named http container port",
		["spec.ports[0].targetPort"]
	)
}

deny[msga] {
	service := input[_]
	service.kind == "Service"

	selector := object.get(service.spec, "selector", {})
	object.get(selector, "app.kubernetes.io/name", "") != "authlab"

	msga := service_alert(
		service,
		"selector app.kubernetes.io/name must be authlab",
		["spec.selector"]
	)
}

deny[msga] {
	service := input[_]
	service.kind == "Service"

	selector := object.get(service.spec, "selector", {})
	object.get(selector, "app.kubernetes.io/component", "") != "web"

	msga := service_alert(
		service,
		"selector app.kubernetes.io/component must be web",
		["spec.selector"]
	)
}

deny[msga] {
	service := input[_]
	service.kind == "Service"

	selector := object.get(service.spec, "selector", {})
	object.get(selector, "app.kubernetes.io/part-of", "") != "secure-deploy-lab"

	msga := service_alert(
		service,
		"selector app.kubernetes.io/part-of must be secure-deploy-lab",
		["spec.selector"]
	)
}

controls.name: Applications credentials in configuration files
controls.description: Attackers who have access to configuration files can steal the stored secrets and use them. This control checks if ConfigMaps or pod specifications have sensitive information in their configuration.
controls.remediation: Use Kubernetes secrets or Key Management Systems to store credentials.

rules.name: rule-credentials-configmap

attributes.m$K8sThreatMatrix: Credential access::Applications credentials in configuration files, Lateral Movement::Applications credentials in configuration files

rules.rule:
package armo_builtins

# fails if config map has keys with suspicious name
deny[msga] {
	configmap := input[_]
    configmap.kind == "ConfigMap"
    # see default-config-inputs.json for list values
    sensitive_key_names := data.postureControlInputs.sensitiveKeyNames
    key_name := sensitive_key_names[_]
    map_secret := configmap.data[map_key]
    map_secret != ""

    contains(lower(map_key), lower(key_name))

    # check that value or key weren't allowed by user
    not is_allowed_value(map_secret)
    not is_allowed_key_name(map_key)

    path := sprintf("data[%v]", [map_key])

	msga := {
		"alertMessage": sprintf("this configmap has sensitive information: %v", [configmap.metadata.name]),
		"alertScore": 9,
		"deletePaths": [path],
        "failedPaths": [path],
        "fixPaths": [],
		"packagename": "armo_builtins",
          "alertObject": {
			"k8sApiObjects": [configmap]
		}
     }
}

# fails if config map has values with suspicious content - not base 64
deny[msga] {
    # see default-config-inputs.json for list values
    sensitive_values := data.postureControlInputs.sensitiveValues
    value := sensitive_values[_]

	configmap := input[_]
    configmap.kind == "ConfigMap"
    map_secret := configmap.data[map_key]
    map_secret != ""

    regex.match(value , map_secret)

    # check that value or key weren't allowed by user
    not is_allowed_value(map_secret)
    not is_allowed_key_name(map_key)

    path := sprintf("data[%v]", [map_key])

	msga := {
		"alertMessage": sprintf("this configmap has sensitive information: %v", [configmap.metadata.name]),
		"alertScore": 9,
		"deletePaths": [path],
       "failedPaths": [path],
        "fixPaths": [],
		"packagename": "armo_builtins",
          "alertObject": {
			"k8sApiObjects": [configmap]
		}
     }
}

# fails if config map has values with suspicious content - base 64
deny[msga] {
    # see default-config-inputs.json for list values
    sensitive_values := data.postureControlInputs.sensitiveValues
    value := sensitive_values[_]

	configmap := input[_]
    configmap.kind == "ConfigMap"
    map_secret := configmap.data[map_key]
    map_secret != ""

    decoded_secret := base64.decode(map_secret)

    regex.match(value , decoded_secret)

    # check that value or key weren't allowed by user
    not is_allowed_value(map_secret)
    not is_allowed_key_name(map_key)

    path := sprintf("data[%v]", [map_key])

	msga := {
		"alertMessage": sprintf("this configmap has sensitive information: %v", [configmap.metadata.name]),
		"alertScore": 9,
		"deletePaths": [path],
       "failedPaths": [path],
        "fixPaths": [],
		"packagename": "armo_builtins",
          "alertObject": {
			"k8sApiObjects": [configmap]
		}
     }
}

is_allowed_value(value) {
    allow_val := data.postureControlInputs.sensitiveValuesAllowed[_]
    regex.match(allow_val , value)
}

is_allowed_key_name(key_name) {
    allow_key := data.postureControlInputs.sensitiveKeyNamesAllowed[_]
    contains(lower(key_name), lower(allow_key))
}

controls.name: Non-root containers
controls.description: Potential attackers may gain access to a container and leverage its existing privileges to conduct an attack. Therefore, it is not recommended to deploy containers with root privileges unless it is absolutely necessary. This control identifies all the pods running as root or can escalate to root.
controls.remediation: If your application does not need root privileges, make sure to define runAsNonRoot as true or explicitly set the runAsUser using ID 1000 or higher under the PodSecurityContext or container securityContext. In addition, set an explicit value for runAsGroup using ID 1000 or higher.

rules.name: non-root-containers
rules.description: fails if container can run as root
rules.remediation: Make sure that the user/group in the securityContext of pod/container is set to an id over 0, or the runAsNonRoot flag is set to true.

controls.name: Allow privilege escalation
controls.description: Attackers may gain access to a container and uplift its privilege to enable excessive capabilities.
controls.remediation: If your application does not need it, make sure the allowPrivilegeEscalation field of the securityContext is set to false.

rules.name: rule-allow-privilege-escalation
rules.description: fails if container allows privilege escalation
rules.remediation: Make sure that the allowPrivilegeEscalation field in the securityContext of pod/container is set to false

controls.name: Immutable container filesystem
controls.description: Mutable container filesystem can be abused to inject malicious code or data into containers. Use immutable (read-only) filesystem to limit potential attacks.
controls.remediation: Set the filesystem of the container to read-only when possible (pod securityContext, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true). If containers application needs to write into the filesystem, it is recommended to mount secondary filesystems for specific directories where application require write access.

rules.name: immutable-container-filesystem
rules.description: fails if container has mutable filesystem
rules.remediation: Make sure that the securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem field in the container/pod spec is set to true

controls.name: Ingress and Egress blocked
controls.description: Disable Ingress and Egress traffic on all pods wherever possible. It is recommended to define restrictive network policy on all new pods, and then enable sources/destinations that this pod must communicate with.
controls.remediation: Define a NetworkPolicy, CiliumNetworkPolicy, or CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy that restricts ingress and egress connections.

rules.name: ingress-and-egress-blocked
rules.description: fails if there are no ingress and egress defined for pod
rules.remediation: Make sure you define ingress and egress policies for all your Pods

controls.name: Automatic mapping of service account
controls.description: Potential attacker may gain access to a pod and steal its service account token. Therefore, it is recommended to disable automatic mapping of the service account tokens in service account configuration and enable it only for pods that need to use them.
controls.remediation: Disable automatic mounting of service account tokens to pods either at the service account level or at the individual pod level, by specifying the automountServiceAccountToken: false. Note that pod level takes precedence.

rules.name: automount-service-account
rules.description: fails if service account and workloads mount service account token by default
rules.remediation: Make sure that the automountServiceAccountToken field on the service account spec if set to false

controls.name: Host PID/IPC privileges
controls.description: Containers should be isolated from the host machine as much as possible. The hostPID and hostIPC fields in deployment yaml may allow cross-container influence and may expose the host itself to potentially malicious or destructive actions. This control identifies all pods using hostPID or hostIPC privileges.
controls.remediation: Remove hostPID and hostIPC from the yaml file(s) privileges unless they are absolutely necessary.

rules.name: host-pid-ipc-privileges
rules.description: Containers should be as isolated as possible from the host machine. The hostPID and hostIPC fields in Kubernetes may excessively expose the host to potentially malicious actions.
rules.remediation: Make sure that the fields hostIPC and hostPID in the pod spec are not set to true (set to false or not present)

controls.name: HostNetwork access
controls.description: Potential attackers may gain access to a pod and inherit access to the entire host network. For example, in AWS case, they will have access to the entire VPC. This control identifies all the pods with host network access enabled.
controls.remediation: Only connect pods to host network when it is necessary. If not, set the hostNetwork field of the pod spec to false, or completely remove it (false is the default). Whitelist only those pods that must have access to host network by design.

rules.name: host-network-access
rules.description: fails if pod has hostNetwork  enabled
rules.remediation: Make sure that the hostNetwork field of the pod spec is not set to true (set to false or not present)

controls.name: Container hostPort
controls.description: Configuring hostPort requires a particular port number. If two objects specify the same HostPort, they could not be deployed to the same node. It may prevent the second object from starting, even if Kubernetes will try reschedule it on another node, provided there are available nodes with sufficient amount of resources. Also, if the number of replicas of such workload is higher than the number of nodes, the deployment will consistently fail.
controls.remediation: Avoid usage of hostPort unless it is absolutely necessary, in which case define appropriate exception. Use NodePort / ClusterIP instead.

rules.name: container-hostPort
rules.description: fails if container has hostPort
rules.remediation: Make sure you do not configure hostPort for the container, if necessary use NodePort / ClusterIP

controls.name: Insecure capabilities
controls.description: Giving insecure or excessive capabilities to a container can increase the impact of the container compromise. This control identifies all the pods with dangerous capabilities (see documentation pages for details).
controls.remediation: Remove all insecure capabilities which are not necessary for the container.

rules.name: insecure-capabilities

controlConfigInputs.name: Insecure capabilities
controlConfigInputs.description: Kubescape looks for these capabilities in containers, which might lead to attackers getting elevated privileges in your cluster. You can see the full list of possible capabilities at https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/capabilities.7.html.

rules.description: fails if container has insecure capabilities
rules.remediation: Remove all insecure capabilities which aren’t necessary for the container.

controls.name: HostPath mount
controls.description: Mounting host directory to the container can be used by attackers to get access to the underlying host. This control identifies all the pods using hostPath mount.
controls.remediation: Remove hostPath mounts unless they are absolutely necessary and use exception mechanism to remove notifications.

rules.name: alert-any-hostpath
rules.rule:
package armo_builtins


deny[msga] {
    pod := input[_]
    pod.kind == "Pod"
    volumes := pod.spec.volumes
    volume := volumes[i]

controls.name: Cluster internal networking
controls.description: If no network policy is defined, attackers who gain access to a container may use it to move laterally in the cluster. This control lists namespaces in which no network policy (NetworkPolicy, CiliumNetworkPolicy, or qualifying CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy) is defined.
controls.remediation: Define Kubernetes NetworkPolicy, CiliumNetworkPolicy, or CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy resources to protect cluster network.

rules.name: internal-networking

attributes.m$K8sThreatMatrix: Lateral Movement::Container internal networking, Discovery::Network mapping

rules.description: lists namespaces in which no network policies are defined

controls.name: Privileged container
controls.description: Potential attackers may gain access to privileged containers and inherit access to the host resources. Therefore, it is not recommended to deploy privileged containers unless it is absolutely necessary. This control identifies all the privileged Pods.
controls.remediation: Remove privileged capabilities by setting the securityContext.privileged to false. If you must deploy a Pod as privileged, add other restriction to it, such as network policy, Seccomp etc and still remove all unnecessary capabilities. Use the exception mechanism to remove unnecessary notifications.

rules.name: rule-privilege-escalation
rules.description: determines if pods/deployments defined as privileged true

controls.name: Container runtime socket mounted
controls.description: Mounting Container runtime socket (Unix socket) enables container to access Container runtime, retrieve sensitive information and execute commands, if Container runtime is available. This control identifies pods that attempt to mount Container runtime socket for accessing Container runtime.
controls.remediation: Remove container runtime socket mount request or define an exception.

rules.name: containers-mounting-docker-socket
rules.description: Check hostpath. If the path is set to one of the container runtime socket, the container has access to container runtime - fail.
